output.headline: Provider-focused growth investor that pays upper-quartile multiples and rarely fails to close, with physician-group and Midwest precedents.
output.differentiator: Pays a median 16.5x, above every other sponsor on the list except Blackstone, and closed 13 of 14 (93%), the best completion rate among the sponsors. [T:record, K:closed_share]
output.why_them: Provider-focused growth equity; pays upper-quartile prices, completes nearly every deal

acquirer_overview.title: Growth equity firm with a provider-heavy, high-completion record
points: Growth equity investor across Technology, Consumer, Financial Services, Healthcare and Life Sciences, with AUM of US$125.3 billion. [P:1, P:2]
Made 14 deals from 2019 to 2024, all control stakes; 13 closed (93%). [T:record, K:control_share, K:closed_share]
9 of 14 deals were in provider services; deal sizes run from $7M to $4,563M, with a median of $158M. [A:angles, T:record]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: A provider specialist with precedents in the target's sub-sector and region
points: Deals in this or neighbouring sub-sectors and a high close rate are modest factors in its likelihood. [S:sector_rel, S:close_rate_s]
Buys for market share (5 of 14 deals, against 19% of all deals in the file) and scale (5 of 14). [M:market_share, M:scale]
Has 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 8 in adjacent provider sub-sectors; its share of own-sub-sector deals is a slight factor against. [T:record, S:sector_share]

precedent_activity.title: Physician-group and Midwest precedents, from $15M to $1,708M
points: Oak Health: $1,708M merger of equals, 2021, 18.8x, in the target's own sub-sector. [D:MA-2021-0066]
Crest Medical Practice: $121M leveraged buyout, 2023, 11.5x; Reliable Medical Associates: $71M, 2021, 13.8x; both physician groups. [D:MA-2023-0499, D:MA-2021-0392]
Harbor Home Health Partners: $15M strategic acquisition in the Midwest, 2022, 16.9x; 2 of its 14 deals were in the target's region. [D:MA-2022-0273, T:record]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible, but the bid needs a platform-style exit
points: 70 comparable deals show 10.7x at the lower quartile, 12.8x median and 15.3x at the 75th percentile; the 75th is the defensible mark. [V:comps]
Target margin of 16.8% sits above the comps' median of 12.9%, supporting upper-quartile pricing; this buyer's own median paid is 16.5x. [V:comps]
At the ask, IRR is 18.7% against a 20% target; maximum price is $193M on the same exit, $216M at a 15.0x platform exit. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: It has no open platform in the sub-sector, so the platform exit is unproven for this buyer. [C:conviction]

risk_flags.title: Thin own-sub-sector record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector, and that share is a slight factor against. [T:record, S:sector_share]
risk_flags.mitigant: 8 deals in adjacent provider sub-sectors, including physician groups. [T:record, K:by_sub_sector]
risk_flags.reality: Its own-sub-sector deal, Oak Health at $1,708M, is far larger than this target. [D:MA-2021-0066]

risk_flags.title: Competitive process
risk_flags.concern: Welsh Carson and GTCR each have more Midwest deals than General Atlantic's 2. [T:record]
risk_flags.mitigant: Its median paid of 16.5x is above both of theirs. [T:record]
risk_flags.reality: Among sponsors on the list, only Blackstone pays a higher median multiple. [T:record]

conviction.rationale: One deal in the target's own sub-sector and 8 in adjacent provider sub-sectors support the fit, but there is no open platform in the sub-sector, which holds the call at Medium. [C:conviction]
